scope: The normalized fundamental SU(2) crossing kernel k_beta(x,y)=exp(-beta*||x^-1*y-1||^2) has constant Haar row integral m(beta). An actual Bochner mean in its constructed Hilbert completion proves that k_beta-m(beta) is positive definite. Tensor-product Hilbert features preserve positivity when this remainder is multiplied by any other positive kernel. Hence inserting one marked crossing multiplies its compact reflection form by at least m(beta), for every continuous complex half-source and any finite collection of other nonnegative-coupling Wilson crossings. The proved inverse-mass bound is m(beta)^-1<=cap(beta)=4*Z_scalar(0)*beta*sqrt(beta)/Gamma(3/2), beta>=3/4. This removes an exponential coupling cost from this integral-form comparison. The application to the actual raw Wilson time-slab kernel retains both spatial potentials and all other temporal kinetic factors: deleting one marked temporal factor gives Q_cut(f)<=cap(beta)*Q_raw(f), for every continuous complex half-source. Specializing to the actually constructed full-transfer ground state psi gives integral psi(u)*K_cut(u,v)*psi(v)<=cap(beta)*||T_full||, with no volume factor and no supplied reflection premise on the ground. The actual normalized stationary raw two-slice law is constructed and proved a probability measure from that same ground and full eigenvalue. For D_e(u,v)=||u_e^-1*v_e-1||^2, its exponential moment is <=cap(beta), and its tail is P(D_e>=t)<=exp(-beta*t)*cap(beta). The background tail is then strengthened to an actual source-sensitive bound. For every continuous real F, E[exp(beta*D_e)*|F(u)|*|F(v)|]<=cap(beta)*M(F). For every continuous gauge-invariant physical F, the exact raw time-increment identity and original full-operator positivity give integral_(D_e>=t) F(u)^2 dnu<=2*loss(F)+2*exp(-beta*t)*cap(beta)*M(F). The coefficient of loss is retained explicitly; no small loss-only absorption is claimed. This is a temporal-gauge defect estimate, not a spatial-plaquette estimate. The spatial omitted-plaquette ground-state reflection identification, actual distant/signed-form control, independent global coercivity and continuum construction remain open.
